title: Everyday chemistry: soaps & detergents
examples: How does soap actually get the dirt off my clothes?
What is the difference between soap and detergent?
Why does soap not work well in certain types of water?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how soap cleans things.
The soap molecule has two different ends that help it clean.
When soap meets grease, the tail sticks into the grease.
This trapping action creates small spheres called micelles.
Hard water contains dissolved minerals that react with soap.

draw.text: Hard water minerals react with soap

explain.say: In real life, washing dishes shows this cleansing action clearly.

faq.q: Does soap only work on grease?
faq.a: No, soap can help lift various types of dirt and grime. It works because of its two different ends.
asks: What kinds of dirt can soap remove?
Is soap only for oil stains?

faq.a: A micelle is a small sphere formed by soap molecules. The grease gets trapped inside this sphere.
asks: How are soap molecules arranged in water?
What is the structure of a micelle?

faq.q: Why is hard water a problem for soap?
faq.a: Hard water minerals react with the soap, causing it to fall out of the solution. This prevents proper cleaning.
asks: Does the water quality affect cleaning?

faq.a: Detergents are often better because they do not react with the minerals in hard water. They clean effectively in many water types.
asks: What is the difference between soap and detergent?
Can detergents clean in hard water?

faq.q: Do I need to worry about the water hardness in my area?
faq.a: If you notice soap scum forming easily, your water might be hard. Using a dedicated detergent can solve this.
asks: How do I test my water hardness?

facts: Soap molecules have a hydrophilic head that dissolves in water.
The hydrophobic tail of the soap sticks into non-polar substances like grease.
Micelles are formed when soap surrounds trapped dirt particles.
Hard water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium ions.

quiz.say: The part of the soap molecule that dissolves in water is called the:
quiz.why: The hydrophilic head is water-loving, which allows the soap to dissolve and spread in water.

wrong.0: A micelle is the structure that forms around the dirt, not the part that dissolves.
wrong.2: This part is oil-loving and stays in the grease, not dissolved in water.
wrong.3: A precipitate is what forms when soap fails to clean in hard water.

quiz.say: What structure is formed when soap traps grease particles?
quiz.why: The micelle is the sphere created by the soap molecules trapping the dirt inside.

wrong.0: A precipitate is a solid that forms when soap reacts with hard water minerals.
wrong.1: This describes the inside of the micelle, not the name of the structure itself.
wrong.2: Soap scum is the visible residue, but the trapping structure is the micelle.

quiz.say: If soap fails to clean well, it is most likely due to:
quiz.why: These minerals react with soap, forming insoluble compounds that prevent cleaning action.

wrong.0: This is a solution, not the cause of the failure. The problem is the water itself.
wrong.2: While grease is the target, the failure is due to the water chemistry, not just the amount of dirt.
wrong.3: While temperature affects solubility, the primary failure mechanism in this context is mineral reaction.
